clue.text: Proud to make a fresh start at Rugby

indicators.note: make here means fashion or form, so the letters of the preceding words are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A proud player restarts a match at Rugby School.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' tells you to rearrange PROUD and TO. In rugby union a drop-out is the drop kick that restarts play from the 22-metre line.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop-out is the restart kick taken from the defending team's 22-metre line in rugby.

clue.text: Absolutely determined there's nothing on the radio due to power cut?

definitions.meaning: firmly resolved, utterly intent on something

definitions.text: there's nothing on the radio due to power cut?
definitions.meaning: a wireless set with no power is lifeless, a set that is dead

explanation.surface: Someone insists the radio is silent because of a blackout.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fully resolved on a course is the idiom; the second reading treats the phrase literally as a lifeless wireless.

clue.text: Lacking siblings, and just 12 months old

definitions.meaning: an only child, with no brothers or sisters
a baby who has just turned a year old

explanation.surface: A baby with no brothers or sisters has just had a first birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: An only child is the sole one; a toddler of a year has an age of exactly a single year.

clue.text: Minister raised in Old Testament? It's obvious

indicators.note: in signals that the turned word sits inside the abbreviation
in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A clergyman is mentioned in the Old Testament, which is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' reverses the minister's title upwards; 'in' places it within the abbreviation for the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done openly and not hidden is plain, the synonym for obvious.

clue.text: With everything to throw around nothing's left

indicators.note: around means the phrase for throwing is wrapped about the other piece

parts.note: to toss is to throw
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone tosses everything about until nothing remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' places TO TOSS round ALL: TOT-ALL-OSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-off where an insured item is wholly destroyed leaves no value remaining.

clue.text: Forcibly puts forward awkward truths to school head

indicators.note: awkward means clumsily arranged, so the word truths is put in a different order
the head of school is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone forces uncomfortable truths on a headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges TRUTHS into THRUST, and 'head' gives S from school.
explanation.definitionFit: To shove something forward with force is the verb sense, here in the third person.

clue.text: Switch lit up bulb

indicators.note: switch means swap around, so the letters of lit up are exchanged into a new order

explanation.surface: Flicking a switch makes a light bulb come on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' rearranges LIT UP; the bulb is a plant's, not a lamp's.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip grows from a bulb, so the plant is an example of a bulb flower.

clue.text: Restore control to the country

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in keep a tight rein
a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A deposed leader wants power over the nation back.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone back into a former position is to bring them back into place.

clue.text: Soldier's stood up girl and married foreign woman

indicators.note: in a down clue stood up means read from the bottom, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier, so the possessive gives GIS
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A soldier jilted his girlfriend and wed a woman from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stood up' looks like a jilting, but in a down clue it reverses the soldier's possessive. GI is an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married lady, Mrs.

clue.text: Seeing about making it genuine

parts.note: seeing that means since, given that
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Seeing something firsthand makes it real.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt and honest without pretence, a synonym for true.

clue.text: Beer intended, we hear, to create disorder

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: ale is beer and meant is intended

explanation.surface: Beer is brewed specifically to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear': ALE MEANT spoken sounds like the answer. Disorder is medical, not rowdiness.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or complaint of the body is a medical disorder.

clue.text: Having a baby, but not coming out with the truth?

definitions.text: not coming out with the truth?

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman denies being in labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confined for childbirth is the old term; the second reading is someone telling fibs while staying indoors.

clue.text: Brief error on the cricket field

parts.note: short means brief
a slip is a small error

explanation.surface: A fielder makes a quick mistake during a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the slips are catching positions beside the wicketkeeper; short slip stands close in.
explanation.definitionFit: A close catching position beside the batter is one of the fielding places in cricket.

clue.text: She goes round the Gold Coast

indicators.note: goes round says one word encircles the other

parts.note: taken as written
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A woman travels round the former Gold Coast colony in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round' signals the container. The Gold Coast is the old colonial name of Ghana, a deliberate distraction: gold here is the heraldic metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Land at the edge of the sea is the coast or seaside.

clue.text: The King has one of them

indicators.note: has means holds within, so the first pieces contain the other

parts.note: taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The monarch owns one of his subjects' possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessive pronoun meaning belonging to those people.

clue.text: Slow worker causing delay

parts.note: to retard is to slow
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: An idle employee holds up the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that slows a process, such as a fire retardant, holds things back.

clue.text: Model paragon, he cares for waifs

indicators.note: model as a verb means shape, so these letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A model citizen looks after homeless children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' rearranges PARAGON HE. The definition describes what the institution does.
explanation.definitionFit: A home for parentless children is an institution that looks after abandoned young.

clue.text: Weak team member sent by coach, perhaps

definitions.meaning: someone carried by the rest of a team
a traveller conveyed on a bus or coach

explanation.surface: A coach drops a weak player from the team.
explanation.definitionFit: A team member who contributes little is carried along; a traveller on a bus is literally carried.

clue.text: Hoist sail to break loose from personal unpleasantness

indicators.note: break loose means come free and scatter, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors hoist sail to escape from an unpleasant shipmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad breath is a personal hygiene problem, a euphemistic unpleasantness.

clue.text: Pope with aspiration to become emperor

parts.note: aspiration is the breathed sound of the letter H
Adrian is the name of several popes

explanation.surface: An ambitious pope hopes to become emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Aspiration looks like ambition but is the H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman emperor who built the wall across northern England.

clue.text: It ends a flight in two ways

definitions.text: It ends a flight in two ways

parts.words: It ends a flight in two ways
parts.note: a plane touching down ends a flight, and the floor at the top of stairs ends a flight of steps

explanation.surface: Something finishes a journey by air in two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Touching down ends an air journey, and a platform at the head of stairs ends a flight of steps.

clue.text: Heather's a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather has the name of a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the Latin genus name of heath plants, and also a female first name.

clue.text: State encouraging one to let matter rest

definitions.text: State encouraging one to let matter rest

parts.words: State encouraging one to let matter rest
parts.note: read as physics, a condition in which matter at rest stays at rest; on the surface, a mood of letting an issue drop

explanation.surface: A mood that tempts someone to drop an issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggishness discourages action, and in physics a body at rest tends to remain at rest.

clue.text: Harsh wind from South and East

parts.note: Auster is the south wind in classical poetry

explanation.surface: A biting wind blows from the south and east.
explanation.walkthrough: Auster is the Roman name for the south wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and stern in manner, a synonym for strict.

clue.text: Spaniard, or anyone else with a present

parts.note: Don is a Spanish gentleman's title
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish man or anyone else brings a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A giver of a gift is someone who donates.

clue.text: The grandeur of the Sergeant's Mess

indicators.note: mess means jumble, so the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: here the possessive s is used as a letter

explanation.surface: The sergeants' mess hall is a grand place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' rearranges SERGEANTS, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificence or eminence, the quality of being great.

clue.text: Consented to give up a vice

indicators.note: give up means let go of, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: agreed means consented
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to give up a bad habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give up' drops A from AGREED.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is one of the seven deadly sins, a classic vice.

clue.text: Two learners in the mountains

parts.note: a tyro is a novice or learner
L is the learner sign on cars

explanation.surface: Two novices head off into the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver shows an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrol is an Alpine region of Austria and Italy, a place set among peaks.

clue.text: Flatter, most sincerely

parts.note: alludes to the saying that copying is the sincerest form of flattery

explanation.surface: A request to praise someone sincerely.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that copying someone is the sincerest way of flattering them.

clue.text: Choke-or throttle?

parts.note: choke and throttle look like car controls but describe strangling someone with a cord

explanation.surface: A question about the controls of a car engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord or wire used to strangle a person, a method of execution.

clue.text: Confined to college after a direction was denied

indicators.note: after means the college word comes after the direction

parts.note: NE is northeast, a compass direction
gated means confined to college as a punishment

explanation.surface: A student is punished after being refused permission.
explanation.walkthrough: Gated is an Oxbridge term for a student confined to college.
explanation.definitionFit: Nullified or cancelled out, which is what refusing something does.

clue.text: Free news publication

definitions.meaning: a press statement issued to the news media

explanation.surface: A newspaper is given away at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to let go; a press statement issued to journalists is also so called.
